title: Have your coding agent map the security risks in your code
summary: Jim Manico published Grim Prompter, a set of prompts that has Claude Code or Codex read a project and write a security risk report citing files and lines.
agent_role: The agent inspects the code read-only, maps trust boundaries and threats, and writes a report with proposed fixes. Humans set scope, check findings, rate risks and approve any test runs.
what_they_did: The author wrote 36 architecture workflows and 29 analysis methods as prompts. You install it as a skill and ask your coding agent for a quick or six-stage review. The agent reads the code without changing it and saves a report plus files for later comparisons.
worth_knowing: The author warns the reports are drafts and do not certify a system is secure. Keep reports out of version control until checked for sensitive details.
prompt: Review [repo path] for security risks. Read the code only; do not run builds, scripts, installs or network calls without my permission. List where data and users cross trust boundaries, likely threats, existing protections and suggested fixes, citing file and line for each. Save the report under threat-model/ and show me the scope first.

curation.rationale: A structured, careful workflow for agents to produce security risk reviews of a codebase, but the README shows no example run or result.
